- `UISheet.swift` — the settle fingerprint (the attached sheet, the modal
  window, the visible window numbers) and the Cancel: a file panel is ended
  with `.cancel`, otherwise the Escape button is pressed, otherwise a lone
  button.
- `AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift` — `select_inspector_tab` (road map 11's
  V3, dev only, wholly under the flag). It picks the inspector's tab and the
  Clip tab's sub-tab through `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and
  `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the strips' own click paths, so a `snapshot_ui`
  capture is what a click shows. It runs on MAIN, not in `devOffMainTools`.
  With no tab it changes nothing, and answers the tab, the active sub-tab
  and the sub-tabs on offer. `section` scrolls a section into view, and the
  answer's `look_thumbnails_pending` says the gallery is still rendering (GR-7).
  Every refusal leaves the inspector as it was.
- `EditorViewController+Look.swift` — Clip ▸ Look ▸ (the eight, a separator,
  None; a checkmark or a dash; spec §11 GR-7) and its validator arm; the
  dev-only launch default `-RCDevLookGalleryDump <folder>` writes each set of
  thumbnails as PNGs for the proof.
- `DevAppearance.swift` — `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, a dev-only launch
  default (road map 11's V3). It sets `NSApp.appearance` from `main.swift`
  before `NSApplicationMain`, so every view is built in that look. A live
  switch leaves colours taken at build time in the launch look, which is why
  `snapshot_ui` refuses `appearance` and names this default instead.
- `AgentServer+Assistant.swift` — `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer`
  (road map 12 A1, dev only, wholly under the flag). Both run off main
  (`devOffMainTools`): one `onMain` resolves the target, the editor and the
  session and sends, answers or stops; then the wait for "not busy" runs
  INSIDE `AgentLane.releasingLock`, polling the phase every 50 ms, because
  the turn's own calls need the lock. The target is resolved BEFORE the
  release, never inside it, where an assistant call may hold
  `callDocument`. `assistant_answer` never opens a session. The answer is
  the state, the question, the text deltas joined and the other events since
  the call — never the key or the model, each `cost` passed through
  `AssistantSpend.toolView` (road map 13 P2). `assistant_send` without `pane`
  sends through `EditorViewController.assistantSend`, so the transcript gets
  the person's line; with `pane` (road map 12 A2) both tools go through the
  Assistant tab's own controls — the composer (its `string` set, any marked
  text committed first) and a `performClick` on Send,
  Allow's or Deny's `mouseDown` with a synthesized click at its centre, Send
  while it reads Stop — refused by name, changing nothing, when the control
  is not in a window or is hidden. The pane check comes before the session
  opens, and the idle check before the click, so a pane send never clicks
  Stop. `stop_after` (seconds, 0.1…600 and less than `timeout`; on
  `assistant_answer` only with `allow`) presses Stop once inside the wait,
  through `editor.assistantStop()`, when the turn is still busy or asking, and
  the answer carries `stopped_ms` (else null).
- `DevAssistantLaunch.swift` — `-RCDevAssistantSend <text>
  -RCDevAssistantReport <path>`, a dev-only launch default (road map 12 A1),
  both from the argument domain alone: after launch, one turn in an untitled
  project with or without the MCP server, a `get_project` through the lane,
  one atomic JSON report (its events' `cost`s through
  `AssistantSpend.toolView`, road map 13 P2), and the session closed. One key
  alone is one stderr line. Installed from `main.swift` after `DevAppearance.apply()`.
- `AgentServer+Snapshot.swift` — `snapshot_ui` (road map 11's V2a, dev only,
  wholly under the flag). It lists the windows, or captures the editor (whole
  or a region), an attached sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel through `cacheDisplay`:
  an image block plus JSON and a PNG, with a `<name>.layout.json` beside it.
  It runs OFF main (`devOffMainTools`): the fill renders through
  `Exporter.renderFrameReported`, the settle sleeps between passes, and every
  AppKit touch is an `onMain` hop. A `defer` unstages on every exit. It works
  with the app inactive and its window occluded (measured, V2a's O rows).
  `appearance` is refused, naming `-RCDevAppearance`.
- `UISnapshot.swift` — `snapshot_ui`'s main-thread half. It resolves the
  window (Settings, Welcome and the recorder panel found in `NSApp.windows`
  by controller class, never `.shared`, which would build them) and the regions (the root's `BarView` and the three pane
  containers), holds the window facts and the listing, and stages the fill
  as an `NSImageView` just above
  `playerHost`, under `safeGuides` and `overlay` (V1's W4a). It also runs one
  `cacheDisplay` pass. `kind(of:)` and `row(_:)` are internal, not private,
  because the menu tool's result rows use them.

unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into
lettered files that keep its number (§4.3 is `04.3a`, `04.3b` and `04.3c`, §5.2 is `05.2a` and `05.2b`, §6 is `06a`, `06b` and `06c`, §7.5 is `07.5a` and `07.5b`, §7.9 is `07.9a`, `07.9b`, `07.9c` and `07.9d`);

# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.

# Frame Job

A screencast video editor. A project is a document of tracks and clips that the core edits through ops; the app and the agent both speak in those ops. This glossary holds the terms the spec and the op table use, sharpened as decisions settle them.

## Language

**Op**:
One edit to a project, named by a row of the op table and applied whole. An op the core understood answers one of exactly three ways: it applies and yields a new project, it is an identity, or it is refused. A request the core could not read at all is none of the three — that is a mistake in the asking rather than an answer about the project.
_Avoid_: command, mutation, action (an action is an animation on a clip)

**Identity**:
An op that was understood and had nothing to change: the project already says what was asked, or the op was handed an empty selection. It leaves the project exactly as it was, makes no undo step, and has nothing to explain — a caller told about a rule here would go looking for one it did not break.
_Avoid_: no-op, failure, "nothing happened" (all three hide the difference from a refusal)

**Refusal**:
A rule declining an op, in that rule's own sentence: which track is locked, which clips still show the media, by how many ticks two clips would overlap and how long the shorter one is. Like an identity it leaves the project exactly as it was and makes no undo step; unlike an identity it says why, and it names what a caller could send instead rather than restating the rule. A refusal is not an error — an error is a request that could not be read.
_Avoid_: error, rejection, failure, "invalid"

**Op table**:
The one list of the ops and their arguments, kept by the core and published by it. A row is an op's name and, per **Argument**, its name, its kind and whether it is required — the STRUCTURE of a call and nothing about its meaning, which stays in the prose beside the ops themselves. Everything downstream — the tool catalog an agent reads, the check that compares the two at startup — reads the table rather than restating it, so an argument is written down once and a row that lies is a failing test rather than a call that goes wrong.
_Avoid_: schema, op list, the op enum (the enum is one implementation of the table)

**Argument**:
One named value an **Op** takes, checked against the op table. An argument is part of the CALL: the core knows what it is — ticks, an id, a boolean, a closed vocabulary — and the app says what it is FOR. Distinct from a **Patch**'s keys, which are part of a VALUE and are checked against the property vocabulary instead: `set_video` takes the two arguments `clips` and `patch`, and everything inside that patch is not an argument at all. A name no tool published is not an argument either: it is refused at the door, naming the tool and what it does take, and never dropped.
_Avoid_: parameter, field, key, option

**Patch**:
A partial object a caller writes to say what to change — a clip's property group, a clip's own name and label, or an action's end state. It merges key by key at every depth; a key set to null clears that key, or removes it from an end state; an array replaces the whole list. A key or value the vocabulary does not have is refused by its dotted path, and never dropped, corrected or clamped. The core is the one that reads it, wherever it came from.
_Avoid_: update, delta, diff, replacement

**Selected action**:
The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing, or none. It is view state, like the playhead and the clip selection: not an edit, not undoable, not saved, and not something an agent sets — an agent names an action by its id. It is chosen by clicking the action's band, or by the playhead ENTERING the action's span; it stays chosen when the playhead leaves, and goes when the clip selection changes, on esc, or on the lane's Clip chip. While one is chosen the fields show and write its END state (spec §11 CI-1, CI-2). Actions are numbered by time order.
_Avoid_: current action, active action, "the action under the playhead" (the playhead no longer decides)

**Graphic**:
A clip whose picture is drawn by code: a **Module** in the package's `graphics/` folder, run per frame with the clip's props, rasterized at the graphic's own size. It is a clip's CONTENT, in the place a media file or an image sits — not an effect, and not a plugin: its code reaches no other clip, no timeline, no model and no file, and the same frame with the same props always draws the same pixels (spec §11 G-1, G-5).
_Avoid_: effect, plugin, overlay, template (a template is a graphic someone else wrote)

**Template**:
A **Module** the app ships, which a person copies into their package with Insert ▸ Graphic…: the file is written into `graphics/` under a free name (`lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`) and a clip drawn by it is placed at the playhead. Once copied it is the package's own module — editing it changes no other package, and no later app version reaches it. Its title in the Graphic dialog is its `meta.name`, read by compiling it once when the dialog first opens, else its file name made a title; the menu bar compiles nothing (spec §11 G-16, G-45).
_Avoid_: preset (a preset is stored settings, not code), sample, built-in graphic

**Category**:
The list a **Module** is filed under in the Graphic dialog: its `meta.category`, else Other. Every bundled **Template** has one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text; the package's own modules are all listed under This Project, first, whatever their own category (spec §11 G-45).
_Avoid_: folder, group, tag

**Graphic package**:
A `.fjgraphic` file the Graphic dialog's Export… writes (`export_graphic` for an agent): a stored zip of a `manifest.json`, one **Module** and only the project fonts and assets the engine was seen to draw, measure, fall back to or resolve while drawing the graphic's frames and its `enum`/boolean variants — never one of the app's bundled fonts. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy; a file name the zip path cannot hold is stored under a tidied one, the manifest keeping the original. Exporting is not an edit. Frame Job opens one (a Finder double-click, the Graphic dialog's From File…, `import_graphic`) to import it: checked, asked about, and its files copied into the front project's `graphics/` under the manifest's names (spec §11 G-46, G-47).
_Avoid_: graphic archive, bundle, template file (a **Template** ships with the app)

**Error card**:
What a **Graphic** draws in its own box when it cannot draw itself — its **Module** is missing or does not compile, or a frame throws, runs past its budget or will not rasterize: dark red, a bright red border, and the graphic's name, its frame and the first diagnostic with its line and column in white. Never the last good frame, which would hide the error from someone scrubbing. An export never delivers one: it is refused before it starts, or stopped at the frame, with no file left (spec §11 G-8).
_Avoid_: slate (the slate is what a layer with no source at all draws), error frame, placeholder

**Module**:
A graphic's source: one JavaScript ES module exporting `render(frame, props, ctx)`, which returns SVG, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. It is compiled once and drawn many times; the standard library is global and nothing can be imported. Many clips may name one module, as many clips share one media file.
_Avoid_: script, component, file (the file holds the module), plugin

**Revision**:
Which text of a **Module** drew a frame: the SHA-256 of its source's bytes, 64 hex digits. Two identical texts are one revision wherever they came from; an edit to the file is a new revision, and an export pins the revision it started with.

content.content: A framejob:// link so a web page can send a graphic to Frame Job in one click [OPEN] At the moment a web page can link to a `.fjgraphic` file (spec §11 G-47). The browser downloads it, and opening the download imports it. The owner chose the extension first and left one-click links for later. **The idea:** a custom URL scheme, for example `Add to Frame Job`. The browser asks "Open Frame Job?". Frame Job then downloads the package itself and hands it to the same import as a Finder open: `GraphicImportSheetController.open(packageAt:)`, the ask-first sheet, and the core reader's checks. **What it needs:** - **The scheme:** `CFBundleURLTypes` in `project.yml`, with an Apple Event or `application(_:open:)` handler. It is claimed only where Finder's type is owned, so a Debug build does not take it (spec §11 V-5). - **The download:** - `https` only, and redirects only to `https`. - A size cap, and a timeout. - The file is saved to a temporary folder, then goes through the ordinary import. - **What the sheet shows:** the host the package came from, beside what G-47's sheet already shows. - **A spec §11 decision** before the code, and a manual-checks row for a real browser click. app/Sources/AudioPane.swift:58: return InspectorSection( app/Sources/AudioPane.swift:160: return InspectorSection( app/Sources/AudioPane.swift:202: return InspectorSection( 59: id: "audio.volume", title: "Volume", 161: id: "audio.fades", title: "Fades", 203: id: "audio.duck", title: "Ducking", 266: id: "audio.noise", title: "Noise Reduction", 321: id: "audio.compressor", title: "Compressor", 409: id: "audio.mix", title: "Mix",

# Walkthroughs — draft road map (TU0–TU4)

**Status: DRAFT for the owner's review (2026-10-31). Nothing is built and no
decision below is recorded in spec §11 yet; TU0 records them.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
should later drive instructional videos.

Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
machinery against **five model walkthroughs** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Walkthroughs are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The walkthrough dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Walkthroughs get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

## 3. Words

**Walkthrough**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project. The
word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: tutorial (which suggests a
separate course with its own sample material), wizard (which suggests the
app makes the choices).

**Step**: one numbered item in a walkthrough. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show
Me does.

## 4. The shape

### 4.1 One source: the guide page's own numbered list

A walkthrough is an ordinary numbered list under a `### Walkthrough:`
heading in its guide page. Each item's machine half sits in an HTML comment
at the end of the item. GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide HTML comments,
so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
apart.

```markdown
### Walkthrough: change a clip's volume
<!-- walkthrough {"id": "audio.volume", "needs": {"clip": {"has_sound": true}}} -->

1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_audio", "args": {"clips": "$selection", "patch": {"volume": 1.5}}}} -->
3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",
   "wait": {"playing": true}, "optional": true} -->
```

A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
the bundle) extracts every walkthrough into one `Walkthroughs.json`
resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.

### 4.2 The step vocabulary

The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.
Every key is optional except that a step has a sentence.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reveal` | Puts the chrome in the state the step needs before the sentence is shown: an inspector `tab`, `sub_tab` and `section` (scrolled into view, its collapsed state not written). |
| `spotlight` | The control the step points at: a closed list of target names (`timeline.clips`, `timeline.bar.add_text`, `toolbar.play`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `inspector.tab.clip`, `section:<id>`, `clip:$created`, `sheet.export.<control>`, …). The list is the app's own table, and the checker reads the names the build publishes. |
| `wait` | What counts as done. It is re-evaluated after each change and after any view-state change. The conditions: `selection` (`min`, `max`, `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`), `changed` (a schema path on the selected clips, compared with its value when the step began), `clips` (`added: n`), `playhead` (`inside: "$selection"`), `range` (`set: true`), `sheet` (`export` up), `queued` (an export job added), `playing`. A step with no `wait` shows Next. |
| `show_me` | The tool call that would satisfy the wait. Its arguments may use the variables below. |
| `optional` | Skip is offered, and finishing the walkthrough does not require this step. |

Variables: `$selection` (the clip ids when the step began), `$created`
(the clips the previous step added), and `{"$pick": {…}}` (the first clip
in time order that matches, for a Show Me that has to choose a clip).

### 4.3 The runner and the coach panel

- **The coach panel.** A small non-activating floating panel beside the
  editor window, the same kind of panel as the recorder. It shows the title,
  "Step 2 of 3", the step's sentence and the buttons **Back**, **Show Me**,
  **Skip** (on optional steps) and **Exit**. When a wait is met, the panel
  shows a tick and moves to the next step. It never takes key focus, so
  typing into an inspector field still goes to the field.
- **The spotlight.** A borderless, click-through child window over the
  editor. It draws a ring around the target's rectangle and follows it when
  the layout moves. Because it is a window, it sits above the Metal and
  `AVPlayerLayer` layers.
- **Needs.** Before step 1, the walkthrough's `needs` are checked against the
  open project. When they are not met, the panel says what is missing and
  how to get it, for example "This walkthrough needs a clip with sound. Open
  a movie first (File ▸ Open…)", and does not start.
- **Where to start one.** **Help ▸ Walkthroughs ▸** has one submenu per guide
  page, filled from `Walkthroughs.json`. A "Try it in Frame Job" link from
  the online guide (`framejob://walkthrough/<id>`) shares #385's URL scheme
  and comes after TU4.

### 4.4 Show Me

Show Me runs the step's `show_me` through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
the Assistant's calls take. Each Show Me edit is an ordinary undo step, and
exiting a walkthrough undoes nothing. Show Me does three jobs:

- it helps a person who is stuck;
- it lets a proof run every walkthrough to the end with no person present;
- it is what auto-play will use for the videos (§8).

## 5. What stays out of the model phase

- Rolling walkthroughs out to every guide page, and the worked examples each
  page still lacks (after TU4, one batch per page).
- A bundled practice project. The model walkthroughs run on the person's
  own project and check `needs` first.
- Auto-play and video capture (§8).
- The `framejob://` link (#385).

## 6. The model set

Five walkthroughs, chosen so that between them they use every step shape the
design has. If these five work, the remaining walkthroughs need content
only, not new machinery.

| # | Walkthrough (guide page) | Steps | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Change a clip's volume** (`audio.md`) | select a clip with sound → Sound ▸ Volume opens → change the level → play | the owner's example: a selection wait, a sub-tab and section reveal, a value-changed wait |
| 2 | **Split a clip** (`editing.md`) | select a clip → move the playhead into it → Clip ▸ Split (⌘T) | a playhead wait (the person scrubs), a menu or key action, a count wait, `$created` |

decision below is recorded in spec §11 yet; TU0 records them.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:

machinery against **five model walkthroughs** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Walkthroughs are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The walkthrough dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Walkthroughs get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

## 3. Words

**Walkthrough**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project. The
word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: tutorial (which suggests a
separate course with its own sample material), wizard (which suggests the
app makes the choices).

**Step**: one numbered item in a walkthrough. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what

so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
apart.

1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},

3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",

A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
the bundle) extracts every walkthrough into one `Walkthroughs.json`
resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.

The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.

|---|---|
| `reveal` | Puts the chrome in the state the step needs before the sentence is shown: an inspector `tab`, `sub_tab` and `section` (scrolled into view, its collapsed state not written). |
| `spotlight` | The control the step points at: a closed list of target names (`timeline.clips`, `timeline.bar.add_text`, `toolbar.play`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `inspector.tab.clip`, `section:<id>`, `clip:$created`, `sheet.export.<control>`, …). The list is the app's own table, and the checker reads the names the build publishes. |
| `wait` | What counts as done. It is re-evaluated after each change and after any view-state change. The conditions: `selection` (`min`, `max`, `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`), `changed` (a schema path on the selected clips, compared with its value when the step began), `clips` (`added: n`), `playhead` (`inside: "$selection"`), `range` (`set: true`), `sheet` (`export` up), `queued` (an export job added), `playing`. A step with no `wait` shows Next. |
| `show_me` | The tool call that would satisfy the wait. Its arguments may use the variables below. |
| `optional` | Skip is offered, and finishing the walkthrough does not require this step. |

(the clips the previous step added), and `{"$pick": {…}}` (the first clip

  "Step 2 of 3", the step's sentence and the buttons **Back**, **Show Me**,
  **Skip** (on optional steps) and **Exit**. When a wait is met, the panel
  shows a tick and moves to the next step. It never takes key focus, so
  typing into an inspector field still goes to the field.

  editor. It draws a ring around the target's rectangle and follows it when

  how to get it, for example "This walkthrough needs a clip with sound. Open

  the online guide (`framejob://walkthrough/<id>`) shares #385's URL scheme
  and comes after TU4.

Multi-phase work (grading tier 2, #257) runs in a worktree OUTSIDE the repo folder (e.g. `~/devel/reelcut-i257`, branch `i257`), one litecode pipeline per phase, and each phase is committed and fast-forward merged into main as soon as its `make gate` passes (check the main tree's `git status` first). **Why:** other sessions edit the main tree, so building there breaks; a long-lived branch drifts and needed a format renumbering at merge (tier 1's 1015 → 15). Merging per phase keeps main current and takes main's real format numbers.

name: litecode-stacked-phases
description: How to run many /litecode pipelines back to back in Reelcut when the user commits only on request - tree-object baselines, reader reviews mapped onto litecode's cast, residue pipelines, rule H
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-09-19/20 the user asked for four road-map items "using /litecode for
each phase" and ten pipelines ran back to back with NO commits between
them, because the user commits only when they ask. What made that work:

- **A baseline per pipeline.** Before each run, write the working tree to a
  git TREE object with a temporary index (`cp .git/index tmp;
  GIT_INDEX_FILE=tmp git add -A; GIT_INDEX_FILE=tmp git write-tree`) and put
  the hash in `request.md`. The run's diff is `git diff <tree>`. Untracked
  files show there as wholly deleted, which is noise: say so in the request,
  and give `git show <tree>:<path> | diff - <path>` for them.
- **A reader review fits litecode's fixed cast**: the designer writes the
  review PLAN (diffs, the questions verbatim, what is already known with
  citations, named mutants of TODAY's tree, never an old binary, which aborts
  the instruments), the implementer is the readers one question at a time and
  fixes survivors, the reviewer is the SCEPTIC told to refute findings and
  break fixes. Record the deviation (sequential readers, one sceptic).
- **litecode never runs a second fix pass.** When the second review still
  says fix-required, run a small RESIDUE pipeline for code or proof changes,
  and close prose nits by hand. Either way nothing stays only in the handoff
  directory: see [[write-findings-into-repo-documents]].
- **Rule H**: any command that could loop without bound (a reverted-fix test,
  a mutant, a stress call) runs under a hard wall-clock limit, kills only the
  process group it started, and records an expiry as the row's answer.
- **The sceptics' verdicts were mostly about the RECORD**: a sentence that
  claimed more than a run printed, a count that did not match its own list, a
  true threshold with a false explanation. Tell every stage: a number is
  written only when a run printed it, and a control is called a CONTROL.
- **A reader's fix is where the worst defect hid**: swapping a snapping
  argument reader for a plain one removed the only ceiling and `Int64.max`
  crashed the app. A fix that changes how an argument is read keeps its
  bounds and is tried at the extremes.

- **A big feature splits into pipelines by what can be PROVED alone**
  (C1, 2026-09-20/21: tolls, pure parts with a probe, the run with its MCP
  proof, the chrome, then live rows and the closing record, then the reader
  review). Draft the next pipeline's `request.md` while the current one
  runs, and finalise it with a "what the last pipeline found that binds you"
  section and the new baseline tree.
- **Subagents will not edit a `CLAUDE.md`, and should not.** A map entry or
  a rule clause a phase makes false is the orchestrator's to apply by hand,
  after the pipeline's last review, recorded in the tree and told to the
  user.
- **When a command is denied, stop that action** — report what is left
  (paths, the one command) and carry on with the rest; never route the same
  deletion through another tool.

**Why:** the user wants every item finished and everything findable, and is
not at the machine to answer between pipelines.
**How to apply:** reuse this shape for any multi-phase request; pass each
pipeline's lessons forward in the next `request.md`. See also
[[roadmap-phases-via-subagents]] and [[user-prefers-my-recommendation]].

lines: +# Tutorials — draft road map (TU0–TU4)
+**Status: DRAFT for the owner's review (2026-10-31). Nothing is built and no
+decision below is recorded in spec §11 yet; TU0 records them.**
+## 1. The ask
+The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
+each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
+a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
+what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
+needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
+"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
+"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
+should later drive instructional videos.
+Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
+machinery against **five model tutorials** (§6), so the owner can try
+them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.
+## 2. What already exists to build on
+- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
+  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
+  examples or steps a machine can run. Tutorials are added to those pages;
+  no second set of docs is started.
+- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
+  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
+  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
+  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
+  to edit.
+- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
+  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
+  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
+  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
+  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
+  preference.
+- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
+  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
+  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
+- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
+  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
+  the app with no person present. The tutorial dev tools (§7) follow
+  their pattern.
+- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
+  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Tutorials get the same kind of
+  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
+  doesn't have fails `make test`.
+## 3. Words
+**Tutorial**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
+can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project. The
+word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: tutorial (which suggests a
+separate course with its own sample material), wizard (which suggests the
+app makes the choices).
+**Step**: one numbered item in a tutorial. Its sentence is what the
+person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
+the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show
+Me does.
+## 4. The shape
+### 4.1 One source: the guide page's own numbered list
+A tutorial is an ordinary numbered list under a `### Tutorial:`
+heading in its guide page. Each item's machine half sits in an HTML comment
+at the end of the item. GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide HTML comments,
+so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
+word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
+apart.
+```markdown
+### Tutorial: change a clip's volume
+<!-- tutorial {"id": "audio.volume", "needs": {"clip": {"has_sound": true}}} -->
+1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
+   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
+   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
+2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
+   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
+   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},
+   "show_me": {"tool": "set_audio", "args": {"clips": "$selection", "patch": {"volume": 1.5}}}} -->
+3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",
+   "wait": {"playing": true}, "optional": true} -->
+A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
+the bundle) extracts every tutorial into one `Tutorials.json`
+resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.
+### 4.2 The step vocabulary
+The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.

# Tutorials — draft road map (TU0–TU4)

**Status: DRAFT for the owner's review (2026-10-31). Nothing is built and no
decision below is recorded in spec §11 yet; TU0 records them.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
should later drive instructional videos.

Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
machinery against **five model tutorials** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Tutorials are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The tutorial dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Tutorials get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

**Tutorial**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project. The
word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: tutorial (which suggests a
separate course with its own sample material), wizard (which suggests the
app makes the choices).

**Step**: one numbered item in a tutorial. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show

The adversarial review raised three objections to the TU0 and TU1 design:

- **Add a title:** the "Show Me" step would be refused on a typical one-track project, because the title would overlap the existing clip.
- **Cross-dissolve:** the tutorial can get stuck when the pair of clips already has a dissolve, since choosing it again changes nothing.
- **Menu steps:** the rule as written can't run a menu-based "Show Me" in the shipped app.

The designer is revising the design against all three now.

# Request — Tutorials road map, phase TU1b: the practice project

## The owner's words (verbatim)

First message (2026-10-31):

> I want to create an extensive set of docs. They should cover every feature of Frame Job, with examples. I also want the feature docs to record steps to run the feature. From those instructions, if a user selects the feature, it will be applied in app. Some features will require the user to do things or input values. For example, increasing the volume of an audio clip requires the user to select a clip, then choose a volume. Running this help script should instruct the user to select a clip, and when they do, open the settings panel for the volume and instruct them to choose a new value. Essentially I want to build tutorial walkthroughs for everything. We can also use them to create instructional videos for later.
> This is obviously a huge amount of work, so I'd like to pick a handful of features to model this feature with. Then we can test and iterate.

Second message, answering the road map's questions:

> 1. Keep
> 2. build a bundled practice project
> 3. Tutorials
>
> Use /litecode to build

## What to build in THIS pipeline

The road map is `designs/tutorials.md`; read it whole, then spec §11
`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` (TU-1..TU-6, written by the last
pipeline). This pipeline builds **TU1b — the practice project** (road map
§5a and §9):

- **The media, made not found.** A generator script checked in beside the
  bundled project, so it carries no third-party footage or music; its
  provenance written down (a `PROVENANCE.md`, as `app/Resources/Models/`
  has). A few megabytes at most. The product keeps no ffmpeg dependency (a
  dev-time generator may use what the repo's tools already use; say which
  and why). The pictures and sound should be pleasant and legible enough to
  film for the instructional videos later (§8) — e.g. distinct scenes a
  viewer can tell apart, sound that makes a volume change and a cross
  dissolve audible — and must not look like real footage of a person or
  brand.
- **The project.** A `.framejob` package (or whatever form the design
  judges right) that meets every model tutorial's `needs` as the five
  tutorials in the guide now state them: at least two clips with sound that
  meet on one track WITHOUT a transition already between them (spec §11's
  `has_transition: false`), room for a title, enough length to set an in/out
  range and export it. Bundled into the app.
- **Opening it.** Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it as an
  untitled copy, so the bundled one is never written and a save asks where
  (spec §11 TU-6). Whatever an agent needs to open it too (spec §7.9's
  parity: a tool, or an existing tool's argument), with its catalog entry
  and guide text. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ also needs to exist as a menu now; the
  per-page tutorial submenus are TU3's, so design the menu so TU3 adds to it
  without rework.
- **A check that every model tutorial's `needs` are met in the bundled
  project**, run by `make test` (no app if it can be done statically through
  the checker the last pipeline built, else over MCP as a proof), so a later
  tutorial or a change to the project that breaks a `needs` fails loudly.
- The guide: the practice project's paragraph in the relevant page(s) and
  the menu row in `menus-and-shortcuts.md`.

## What the last pipeline found that binds you

(Filled in by the orchestrator when TU0+TU1 closes.)

## Binding rules

- The repo's root `CLAUDE.md` and `app/CLAUDE.md` (and `core/CLAUDE.md` if
  you touch Rust) govern. In particular: file caps (~600 lines, new files
  400), the FFI lockstep if any `rc_*` is added, every user-visible change
  edits its `docs/guide/` page, decisions go in spec §11 BEFORE the code (add
  to the tutorials file), every new menu item needs its rows in
  `UIMenuTable.swift` and `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`.
- **Never edit any `CLAUDE.md`.** List every edit a CLAUDE.md owes under
  "CLAUDE.md edits owed" in your notes; the orchestrator applies them.
- **Work only in this worktree:**
  `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/tutorial-handler`
  (branch `worktree-tutorial-handler`). Never `cd` to or run git against the
  main checkout `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob`. Keep shell commands
  plain (no `git -C`, no compound cd chains to other trees): the session's
  sandbox refuses commands it cannot verify stay in the worktree. Do not
  commit; the orchestrator commits after the review.
- `tools/proof/media/` is in place (gitignored).
- Verification per root CLAUDE.md "Verification": targeted checks in the
  loop, `make app-debug` and an MCP drive for the menu item and the agent
  path, then `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete (foreground under
  600 s if warm; background with a bound if cold, waited on once).
- A number is written in a record only when a run printed it. The phase's
  record goes in `designs/tutorials.md`'s "Record" section.
- Residue: done now, or filed as a GitHub issue (`gh issue create --label
  ai-drafted --label low-priority …`) — never left only in the handoff folder.
- Person-only checks (how the practice media looks and sounds) are rows in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- If a choice is genuinely the owner's, write it under "Owner choices" with
  your recommendation and proceed with the recommendation.

# Request — Tutorials road map, phase TU1b: the practice project

## The owner's words (verbatim)

First message (2026-10-31):

> I want to create an extensive set of docs. They should cover every feature of Frame Job, with examples. I also want the feature docs to record steps to run the feature. From those instructions, if a user selects the feature, it will be applied in app. Some features will require the user to do things or input values. For example, increasing the volume of an audio clip requires the user to select a clip, then choose a volume. Running this help script should instruct the user to select a clip, and when they do, open the settings panel for the volume and instruct them to choose a new value. Essentially I want to build tutorial walkthroughs for everything. We can also use them to create instructional videos for later.
> This is obviously a huge amount of work, so I'd like to pick a handful of features to model this feature with. Then we can test and iterate.

Second message, answering the road map's questions:

> 1. Keep
> 2. build a bundled practice project
> 3. Tutorials
>
> Use /litecode to build

## What to build in THIS pipeline

The road map is `designs/tutorials.md`; read it whole, then spec §11
`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` (TU-1..TU-6, written by the last
pipeline). This pipeline builds **TU1b — the practice project** (road map
§5a and §9):

- **The media, made not found.** A generator script checked in beside the
  bundled project, so it carries no third-party footage or music; its
  provenance written down (a `PROVENANCE.md`, as `app/Resources/Models/`
  has). A few megabytes at most. The product keeps no ffmpeg dependency (a
  dev-time generator may use what the repo's tools already use; say which
  and why). The pictures and sound should be pleasant and legible enough to
  film for the instructional videos later (§8) — e.g. distinct scenes a
  viewer can tell apart, sound that makes a volume change and a cross
  dissolve audible — and must not look like real footage of a person or
  brand.
- **The project.** A `.framejob` package (or whatever form the design
  judges right) that meets every model tutorial's `needs` as the five
  tutorials in the guide now state them: at least two clips with sound that
  meet on one track WITHOUT a transition already between them (spec §11's
  `has_transition: false`), room for a title, enough length to set an in/out
  range and export it. Bundled into the app.
- **Opening it.** Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it as an
  untitled copy, so the bundled one is never written and a save asks where
  (spec §11 TU-6). Whatever an agent needs to open it too (spec §7.9's
  parity: a tool, or an existing tool's argument), with its catalog entry
  and guide text. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ also needs to exist as a menu now; the
  per-page tutorial submenus are TU3's, so design the menu so TU3 adds to it
  without rework.
- **A check that every model tutorial's `needs` are met in the bundled
  project**, run by `make test` (no app if it can be done statically through
  the checker the last pipeline built, else over MCP as a proof), so a later
  tutorial or a change to the project that breaks a `needs` fails loudly.
- The guide: the practice project's paragraph in the relevant page(s) and
  the menu row in `menus-and-shortcuts.md`.

## Binding rules

- The repo's root `CLAUDE.md` and `app/CLAUDE.md` (and `core/CLAUDE.md` if
  you touch Rust) govern. In particular: file caps (~600 lines, new files
  400), the FFI lockstep if any `rc_*` is added, every user-visible change
  edits its `docs/guide/` page, decisions go in spec §11 BEFORE the code (add
  to the tutorials file), every new menu item needs its rows in
  `UIMenuTable.swift` and `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`.
- **Never edit any `CLAUDE.md`.** List every edit a CLAUDE.md owes under
  "CLAUDE.md edits owed" in your notes; the orchestrator applies them.
- **Work only in this worktree:**
  `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/tutorial-handler`
  (branch `worktree-tutorial-handler`). Never `cd` to or run git against the
  main checkout `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob`. Keep shell commands
  plain (no `git -C`, no compound cd chains to other trees): the session's
  sandbox refuses commands it cannot verify stay in the worktree. Do not
  commit; the orchestrator commits after the review.
- `tools/proof/media/` is in place (gitignored).
- Verification per root CLAUDE.md "Verification": targeted checks in the
  loop, `make app-debug` and an MCP drive for the menu item and the agent
  path, then `make gate` ONCE when the code is complete (foreground under
  600 s if warm; background with a bound if cold, waited on once).
- A number is written in a record only when a run printed it. The phase's
  record goes in `designs/tutorials.md`'s "Record" section.
- Residue: done now, or filed as a GitHub issue (`gh issue create --label
  ai-drafted --label low-priority …`) — never left only in the handoff folder.
- Person-only checks (how the practice media looks and sounds) are rows in
  `docs/manual-checks.md`.
- If a choice is genuinely the owner's, write it under "Owner choices" with
  your recommendation and proceed with the recommendation.

  - **Bundle layout.** The project ships as `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`. Its repo source is `app/Resources/Practice/Practice Project.framejob/`, added to `project.yml` as a folder reference. `PROVENANCE.md` and a `SHA256SUMS` file sit beside the package and are not bundled.

It is compiled over `app/Sources` through `swift_build.build()` (the `applelog_writer` precedent) and driven by `tools/practice/make_practice.py`.
  - **Content.** Three 8 s scenes at 1280×720, 30 fps (Dawn, Sea, Night), each with its own chord and drawn in the two OFL fonts already in `app/Resources/Fonts`. Each is placed as a 6 s clip with 1 s of spare footage at each end, back to back on Track 1 (0–18 s, no transition), with a 4,000,000-byte cap on the package.

  - **Media paths.** `project.json` stores placeholder paths that never resolve. On open, the existing `reanchoringConsolidatedMedia` repair points them at the package's own `media/` folder.
  - **Opening it.** `PracticeProject.open()` copies the order of `untitled(around:)`: open an untitled document, set its name to "Practice Project", call `read(from:ofType:)` on the bundled package, then show the window. It does not touch `ProjectDocument.swift`, which is 1334 lines.
    - It deliberately avoids `duplicateDocument` and `init(for:withContentsOf:)`, which would make the app bundle the autosave location.
    - The copy opens clean; a save asks where, and the saved copy points at the media inside the app. TU-7 records this as an accepted risk: moving the app breaks those links until Relink or Consolidate Media.
  - **Agent path.** `new_project` gains a `practice` argument rather than a new tool. A new tool would change the "one hundred and two tools" count in `CLAUDE.md`, the spec and the gate comment. `AgentCatalog.swift` must stay at or under 600 lines (it is 579 now).

  - **The four nits.** Each has a selftest case where it is a refusal: a refused tutorial comment now counts as one problem, `<!-- tutorial` inside a list item is refused, and a duplicate id is reported at line 7. The docstring fix needs no case. The selftest goes to 19 cases plus CONTROL (5 new; 3 cover the practice checks).

  - **New MCP proof.** `tools/proof/practice_project_proof.py` covers both doors. It also confirms the bundled package is never written: its files match `SHA256SUMS` before and after edits and saves.

Full is `make gate`, then the practice and graphics-menu proofs against Release. Four mutants are listed.

    - `app/CLAUDE.md` entries: `TutorialClipFacts.swift`, `PracticeProject.swift`, and `+Tutorials` in the AppDelegate family line.
  - **Owner choice.** The scenes' look and sound are built as the spec describes, and the owner judges them in the new manual check TUT-1.

# Orchestrator objection (a fourth, beside 02-objections.md)

**4. correctness / missing-edge-case — a saved practice copy must not point
into the app bundle.** 01-spec.md accepts, as TU-7's risk, that a saved copy's
media resolve to the files inside `Frame Job.app` and break only if the app
moves. That case is commoner than it reads:

- **App Translocation.** A first-run person who opens the downloaded app
  from `~/Downloads` (or from the DMG) without moving it runs it from a
  randomised read-only path under `/private/var/folders/…/AppTranslocation/`,
  new on each launch. The practice project is exactly what a first-run person
  opens, so their saved copy's media links break on the next launch.
- **Updates and moves.** Sparkle replaces the bundle; a person may move or
  rename the app; a later version may change or drop a practice file.

**Fix (recommended):** a practice copy owns its media once it has a file —
the first save of a practice copy (Save, Save As, and `new_project
{practice: true, path: …}`) copies the practice media into the saved package
(the existing Consolidate machinery, or the same copy it does; the media are
a few MB), so the saved project references only files inside itself. Record
it in TU-7 instead of the accepted risk, and add a proof row that the saved
package's media paths are inside the saved package and that it reopens with
no missing media after the bundled copy is out of reach (e.g. its paths
checked not to start with the app bundle's path).

content.text:
The designer is revising TU1b against four objections:

- **The copy's name:** after you save it, the window title and the agent's answers would still say "Practice Project" instead of the file's name.
- **Opening the bundled package directly:** an agent's `open_project`, or a double-click after Show Package Contents, could write into the app and break its signature.
- **A proof step:** one proof step would edit the wrong untitled copy.
- **My objection:** a saved practice copy would point at media inside the app bundle. That breaks for a first-run user who runs the app straight from Downloads, because macOS runs it from a random path that changes each launch. The fix is to copy the practice media into the project on its first save.

# Request — Tutorials road map, phase TU2: the runner, with no chrome

## The owner's words (verbatim)

First message (2026-10-31):

> I want to create an extensive set of docs. They should cover every feature of Frame Job, with examples. I also want the feature docs to record steps to run the feature. From those instructions, if a user selects the feature, it will be applied in app. Some features will require the user to do things or input values. For example, increasing the volume of an audio clip requires the user to select a clip, then choose a volume. Running this help script should instruct the user to select a clip, and when they do, open the settings panel for the volume and instruct them to choose a new value. Essentially I want to build tutorial walkthroughs for everything. We can also use them to create instructional videos for later.
> This is obviously a huge amount of work, so I'd like to pick a handful of features to model this feature with. Then we can test and iterate.

Second message, answering the road map's questions:

> 1. Keep
> 2. build a bundled practice project
> 3. Tutorials
>
> Use /litecode to build

## What to build in THIS pipeline

The road map is `designs/tutorials.md`; read it whole, then spec §11
`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` (TU-1..TU-7). This pipeline builds
**TU2 — the runner, with no chrome** (road map §4.2–§4.4, §7, §9):

- **The model:** `Tutorials.json` (the bundled resource the "Write
  Tutorials" step writes) read into typed tutorials and steps, refusing
  nothing the checker already accepts and accepting nothing it refuses.
- **The runner**, one per editor window at most: start a tutorial by id
  against that window's project; check its `needs` before step 1 and refuse
  in one sentence that names what is missing (the panel that shows this
  sentence and offers the practice project is TU3's; the runner owns the
  sentence); per step apply `reveal` (through the inspector's own click
  paths, writing no preference), hold the `spotlight` target name for TU3,
  evaluate `wait` after every document change and view-state change
  (selection, playhead, range, inspector tab, playing, sheet, export
  started) — event-driven where the app posts, with any polling justified;
  resolve the variables at the moments TU-2 defines; advance when a wait is
  met; Back, Skip (optional steps only), Next (steps with no wait) and Exit.
- **Show Me:** the tool form through `AgentServer.execute` with ordinary
  undo (as the Assistant's calls), the menu form through the built menu
  bar's own validated item (spec §11 TU-3) — not through any dev tool, so it
  works in Distribution. A Show Me that is refused or errors leaves the step
  where it was and says why.
- **The dev tools** (compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, counted as dev
  tools by `tools/proof/dev_tools.py`): `tutorial_start {id}`,
  `tutorial_state`, `tutorial_step {action: show_me|next|back|skip}`,
  `tutorial_exit`, with catalog rows and the parity check satisfied. The
  product way to start one (Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ …) is TU3's.
- **`tools/proof/tutorial_proof.py`** over MCP, starting from the practice
  project (`new_project {practice: true}` from TU1b): each of the five model
  tutorials run (a) as a person — every wait met with the ordinary tools
  (`set_selection`, `set_audio`, `set_playhead`, `set_range`,
  `perform_menu_item`, `set_video`, `set_text`, …) and the runner read to
  advance and the inspector read to show the revealed tab, sub-tab and
  section (`select_inspector_tab` with no tab); (b) by Show Me alone to the
  end, with the project read back through `get_project`; and (c) on an empty
  project, the `needs` sentence. Plus rows for Back, Skip, Exit, a refused
  Show Me, and an undo after a Show Me. Its README row.

## What the last pipelines found that binds you

(Filled in by the orchestrator when TU1b closes.)

## Binding rules

- The repo's root `CLAUDE.md` and `app/CLAUDE.md` govern. In particular: file
  caps (~600 lines, new files 400; a file at the cap gives something up as a
  pure move before it takes anything on), frozen files take wiring only,
  every new dev tool goes through the gate and the parity check, decisions go
  in spec §11 BEFORE the code (add to the tutorials file), every user-visible
  change edits its `docs/guide/` page.
- **Never edit any `CLAUDE.md`.** List every edit a CLAUDE.md owes under
  "CLAUDE.md edits owed"; the orchestrator applies them.
- **Work only in this worktree:**
  `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/tutorial-handler`
  (branch `worktree-tutorial-handler`). Never `cd` to or run git against the
  main checkout. Keep shell commands plain (no `git -C`, no compound cd
  chains to other trees). Do not commit; the orchestrator commits.
- Verification per root CLAUDE.md: targeted checks in the loop, `make
  app-debug` and the proof against Debug while building, then `make gate`
  ONCE when the code is complete, then the proof run whole once against
  Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release`). Launch your own instance and kill only
  that pid. `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` prints nothing before
  any proof is trusted. Mutants on the decisions this phase adds (3–8).
- A number is written in a record only when a run printed it. The phase's
  record goes in `designs/tutorials.md`'s "Record" section.
- Residue: done now, or filed as a GitHub issue (`gh issue create --label
  ai-drafted --label low-priority …`).
- If a choice is genuinely the owner's, write it under "Owner choices" with
  your recommendation and proceed with the recommendation.

### TU1b (2026-10-31)

**Landed.** Spec §11 TU-7, recorded before the code, and TU-2 (3)'s
definitions of `has_sound` and `has_pixels`. The practice project:
`tools/practice/` (`practice_media.swift` draws and encodes one scene with
AVFoundation, Core Graphics and Core Text; `practice_generator.swift` writes
the three, probes them with `MediaImporter.probeBlocking` and builds
`project.json` through the core's own ops; `make_practice.py` builds it through
`swift_build`, replaces the package and writes `SHA256SUMS`), the generated
`app/Resources/Practice/Practice Project.framejob` (Dawn, Sea, Night: three
6 s clips with 1 s handles back to back on Track 1, no transition) with its
`PROVENANCE.md`, bundled by `project.yml`. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice
Project (`AppDelegate+Tutorials.swift`, `PracticeProject.open()`: an untitled
copy titled "Practice Project") and its mirror `new_project {practice:
true}`; a saved copy carries its media into its own package
(`ProjectDocument+PracticeMedia.swift`'s `write(to:…)`, fed by the save
funnel in `+CacheSaves`), and Consolidate relinks a carried file rather than
copying it; an open of anything inside the app is a practice copy
(`ProjectDocumentController`) or a refusal (`open_project`).
`TutorialClipFacts.swift` answers the clip filter's five keys per clip;
`tutorial_probe.swift` reads the package as the app opens it and
`tutorial_check.py`'s `check_practice` holds every tutorial's `needs`, the
media and `SHA256SUMS` in `make test`. `practice_project_proof.py` over MCP.
TU1's four review nits fixed, each a selftest case where it is a refusal.
No op, no `rc_*`, no format bump, no new tool.

**Measured.** `make_practice.py`: the package is 1,497,141 bytes (Dawn.mov
438,263, Sea.mov 416,277, Night.mov 637,027, project.json 5,574; cap
4,000,000); ffmpeg's volumedetect on Sea.mov: max −14.9 dB.
`tutorial_check --selftest: 20/20 passed`; `tutorial_check: 5 tutorials,
17 steps, 0 problems`. `make typecheck` 0 errors and the four baseline
warnings. `make gate`: `gate: PASS 245s` (test 125 s, app 109 s). On Release:
`practice_project_proof.py` `scores: 10 pass, 0 fail of 10`;
`graphics_menu_proof.py` `44/44 checks passed`. Mutants: `followsClip`'s `<=`
as `<` and `hasTransition` inverted each failed `tutorial_check` (the cross
dissolve's `needs` unmet); the `openPracticeProject:` row dropped failed
`v2_menu.py` H2; `newProject` ignoring `practice` failed P1 (and P5); §F's
`write` returning after `super` failed P4 (no media carried, paths in the
bundle) and R1; `openProject`'s inside-the-app refusal removed failed O1, and
N1 caught the reopened bundle's `cache/` written into the Debug app. The
funnel's `displayName = nil` removed SURVIVED: P4 and P5 still answered the
file's name, because AppKit itself drops a set `displayName` when a save
gives the document its file on macOS 26.5.1; the line stays as a guard no
instrument can fail today. AppKit's `displayName` for a saved package shows
its extension on this host (`saved.framejob`), so the rows take the file's
name with or without it.

**Owed.** #425 (an untitled practice copy restored from an autosave
elsewhere after the app moved has missing media until Relink, TU-7's accepted
risk). Person checks TUT-1 (the media's look and sound, the owner's choice of
scenes) and TUT-2 (Save asks where, the saved copy after the app moves, the
Finder door) in `docs/manual-checks.md`. The CLAUDE.md edits are listed in
the pipeline's notes for the orchestrator.

# Request — Tutorials road map, phase TU2: the runner, with no chrome

## The owner's words (verbatim)

First message (2026-10-31):

> I want to create an extensive set of docs. They should cover every feature of Frame Job, with examples. I also want the feature docs to record steps to run the feature. From those instructions, if a user selects the feature, it will be applied in app. Some features will require the user to do things or input values. For example, increasing the volume of an audio clip requires the user to select a clip, then choose a volume. Running this help script should instruct the user to select a clip, and when they do, open the settings panel for the volume and instruct them to choose a new value. Essentially I want to build tutorial walkthroughs for everything. We can also use them to create instructional videos for later.
> This is obviously a huge amount of work, so I'd like to pick a handful of features to model this feature with. Then we can test and iterate.

Second message, answering the road map's questions:

> 1. Keep
> 2. build a bundled practice project
> 3. Tutorials
>
> Use /litecode to build

## What to build in THIS pipeline

The road map is `designs/tutorials.md`; read it whole, then spec §11
`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` (TU-1..TU-7). This pipeline builds
**TU2 — the runner, with no chrome** (road map §4.2–§4.4, §7, §9):

- **The model:** `Tutorials.json` (the bundled resource the "Write
  Tutorials" step writes) read into typed tutorials and steps, refusing
  nothing the checker already accepts and accepting nothing it refuses.
- **The runner**, one per editor window at most: start a tutorial by id
  against that window's project; check its `needs` before step 1 and refuse
  in one sentence that names what is missing (the panel that shows this
  sentence and offers the practice project is TU3's; the runner owns the
  sentence); per step apply `reveal` (through the inspector's own click
  paths, writing no preference), hold the `spotlight` target name for TU3,
  evaluate `wait` after every document change and view-state change
  (selection, playhead, range, inspector tab, playing, sheet, export
  started) — event-driven where the app posts, with any polling justified;
  resolve the variables at the moments TU-2 defines; advance when a wait is
  met; Back, Skip (optional steps only), Next (steps with no wait) and Exit.
- **Show Me:** the tool form through `AgentServer.execute` with ordinary
  undo (as the Assistant's calls), the menu form through the built menu
  bar's own validated item (spec §11 TU-3) — not through any dev tool, so it
  works in Distribution. A Show Me that is refused or errors leaves the step
  where it was and says why.
- **The dev tools** (compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, counted as dev
  tools by `tools/proof/dev_tools.py`): `tutorial_start {id}`,
  `tutorial_state`, `tutorial_step {action: show_me|next|back|skip}`,
  `tutorial_exit`, with catalog rows and the parity check satisfied. The
  product way to start one (Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ …) is TU3's.
- **`tools/proof/tutorial_proof.py`** over MCP, starting from the practice
  project (`new_project {practice: true}` from TU1b): each of the five model
  tutorials run (a) as a person — every wait met with the ordinary tools
  (`set_selection`, `set_audio`, `set_playhead`, `set_range`,
  `perform_menu_item`, `set_video`, `set_text`, …) and the runner read to
  advance and the inspector read to show the revealed tab, sub-tab and
  section (`select_inspector_tab` with no tab); (b) by Show Me alone to the
  end, with the project read back through `get_project`; and (c) on an empty
  project, the `needs` sentence. Plus rows for Back, Skip, Exit, a refused
  Show Me, and an undo after a Show Me. Its README row.
